appraisal_events.evidence: « Andrée avait pourtant bien plus qu'elle l'intelligence des choses du cœur, le raffinement dans la gentillesse » ... « on aurait dit qu'au fond de sa nature, il n'y avait rien de cette bonté qu'elle manifestait à tout moment » ... « du moindre des riens ... qui eussent pu m'unir à Albertine, elle ne fit jamais usage » ... « Hélas si, elle sera immariable ! » ... « les amis pleins de tact, une forte dose de dissimulation. Je pensais que tel était le cas pour Andrée sans en être cependant absolument sûr. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator builds an elaborate encomium of Andrée's tact, delicacy and devoted friendship and then systematically converts each virtue into evidence of dissimulation and concealed hostility toward his love for Albertine. The praise is real but the passage's structure makes it the vehicle of her local demotion rather than her elevation.

appraisal_events.evidence: « je n'étais pas certain de la bonté profonde de la première comme je le fus plus tard de celle de la seconde » ... « Je savais maintenant que j'aimais Albertine » ... « ma chambre me redevenait réelle et chère, se renouvelait, car j'en regardais et en appréciais chaque meuble avec les yeux d'Albertine » ... « elle me laissa heureux, mais plus affamé d'elle encore que je n'étais au départ »
appraisal_events.explanation: Albertine is raised on two converging fronts: she is retrospectively credited with the deep goodness Andrée is suspected of lacking, and the narrator's love for her crystallizes into an avowed fact that reorganizes his whole perception of his room around her gaze.

status_effects.explanation: Her acknowledged superiority in tact and refinement is locally outweighed by the narrator's suspicion that her goodness is a surface performance masking concealed anger and quiet obstruction.

She gains decisive emotional leverage: the narrator's love is now avowed to himself, his room is revalued through her eyes, and he ends the outing hungrier for her than before while she is asked for nothing.
Though she is called frivolous, poor and incapable of Andrée's refinements, the comparison finally favors her because the narrator vouches for her deep goodness and only doubts Andrée's.

The crystallized love leaves him dependent rather than fulfilled: he conceals his feeling as strategy, stage-manages the carriage seating to seem resigned, and comes away only more starved, with nothing yet asked or granted.

ambiguities: The indictment of Andrée is explicitly hedged in the text itself (« par hasard peut-être », « je ne jurerais pas », « sans en être cependant absolument sûr »), yet the paragraph's architecture and its aside on tact as dissimulation clearly guide the judgment; it is read here as an endorsed but deliberately unproven suspicion rather than a neutral report.

The comparative verdict favoring Albertine rests on retrospective narration (« comme je le fus plus tard »), so part of the local elevation is imported from knowledge the scene itself does not yet possess.
